entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Cornificius, a member of the plebeian gens Cornificia, was a Roman politician and consul in 35 BC.

Born in Rome, Italy, around 90 BCE, Cornificius rose through the ranks of Roman politics, eventually becoming consul in 35 BC. As consul, he played a crucial role in shaping the Roman government's response to the growing threat of the Parthian Empire. His efforts helped secure a crucial victory at the Battle of Rhyndacus in 37 BC, which marked a turning point in the Roman-Parthian conflict.

Despite his significant contributions to Roman politics, Cornificius's legacy is somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, such as Cicero and Julius Caesar. However, his appointment as consul in 35 BC remains an important milestone in the history of the Roman Republic, highlighting the complexities and nuances of Roman politics during this period.

The legacy of Lucius Cornificius can be seen in the continued evolution of the Roman Republic, as well as the impact of his policies on the Roman-Parthian conflict. His efforts helped pave the way for future Roman conquests in the region, cementing Rome's position as a dominant world power.
